Twenty-six comments

Liz Carroll’s #1

This is the first of 2 fine un-named reels composed by Liz Carroll, and recorded by Cathal Hayden, twice. I’m not aware of them ever having been recorded by anyone else, even Liz herself. “Session” contributer Niall Kenny used to play them on flute when in an Edinburgh band called “Miro” in the 1980s.
Both reels were transcribed years ago by fiddler and would-be flute player :) Ged Palmer from Liverpool, one-time resident of Aberdeen. I think there were a few minor mistakes which I hope I have corrected. I’ll post the other reel in the next few days.
Dow – you might like to check this, as it appears you have Cathal Hayden’s recording “Handed Down”, which was the source of Ged’s transcriptions.

↳ Posted by Kenny on June 30th, 2008.

This transcription seems pretty sound to me. On his “Handed Down recording”, first time through, CH plays bar 6 of the A-part as |DG,A,G, B,EDB,| and thereafter as |DG, (3G,G,G, DG,B,D|. Bar 1 of the B-part is as you have it 1st time through, but thereafter it’s the same as bar 5, and played as |EAcA eAcA|. The last turnaround of the B-part is |GEDB, CA,B,D|. Obviously there are other minor variations to the tune each time through. On his “Cathal Hayden” recording, he plays it almost the same, but with a few differences. Bar 2 of the A-part is |G,2A,G, DG,B,G,|. Bar 5 is |EAAG EAGE|. Bars 1 and 5 of the B-part are |EA (3AAA eABA|.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on June 30th, 2008.

Apology

Please accept my apology, “Bjcomm96” - you’re quite correct. I didn’t think I still had the Carroll/McGuire recording [ I did have the LP once upon a time ], but I found the track on an old cassette tape. It is, as you say, the same tune, but Cathal Hayden plays it very much in his own style, so much so that I never made the connection, which you did, and fair play to you for that. I’ll correct the title to yet another “Finbarr Dwyer” tune, and remove the Liz Carroll title, as only CH seems to have recorded it with that name.

Liz Carroll’s (per Zoë Conway)

Zoë Conway calls this tune Liz Carroll’s and plays it after Charlie Lennon’s tune Sailing In (in E) on her 2002 self-titled album (see https://thesession.org/recordings/391?tune_id=3178). I haven’t found it in Liz’s first volume of collected tunes (published 2010) nor elsewhere on The Session even searching with phrases in ABC. I’d appreciate any other info about the tune.
